name: Entity Field Fetch
description: Provides a field type that fetches (mirrors) a field value from another entity — a chosen node, term, or paragraph — onto the entity it is placed on, for centralized/shared content that rides along like an entity reference.

suggests.drupal/paragraphs: Use a specific paragraph on the source entity as the fetch target.
suggests.drupal/graphql: Expose the computed fetched data through the bundled GraphQL field.
suggests.drupal/markdown: Render the module README as HTML on its help page.

project_description:
When you need for a field or paragraph on one node or term to be the source of content for every node on another content type, this module can get you there. It allows you to have a workflow for centralized content.

How does it work? Any node or term can be created to serve as the source of the centralized content. An Entity Field Fetch field is then added to an entity (content type, vocabulary, paragraph) that should display the centralized content. The Entity Field Fetch field goes and gets (fetches) the source content from the centralized content entity and displays it on both view and edit modes for the destination entity. The source data also rides along with the destination entity in a manner similar to an entity reference so it works with entity loads and data APIs.

Alternate approaches? Blocks can work for shared content, however their workflow is more abstract and the editorial experience is not ideal; the other drawback is that the data does not belong to the entity, which can complicate decoupled approaches. A markup field edits the data in the field setting, which makes workflow and revisions impossible to set up.

Setup: enable Entity Field Fetch; create a node or term to hold the source content; add a field of type Entity Field Fetch field to the content type/vocabulary/paragraph that should display it, and configure the target entity type (node or term), the target entity id (nid or tid), the field machine name to fetch, and optionally the paragraph id/UUID. When you view or edit any entity that has this field, you will see the content from the centralized source. The content displayed is cached based on the central content source, so updating the source refreshes the cache.
